    0. Purpose And Scope

    This plan documents only new implementation work.

    It does not inventory, redesign, or reimplement metrics that already work. Existing fields appear only when they are:

    • formula inputs for a new metric;
    • source data required for historical backfill;
    • anchors that define the exact canonical location of new report fields.

    The new work has four parts:

    1. Complete the mandatory shared-helper ownership remediation defined in Section 0.1.
    2. Add new report-calculated cross-fold, investor-summary, and Alpha RC selectivity outputs.
    3. Add new persisted investor, trade-distribution, cost, turnover, exposure, and operational risk-gate metrics.
    4. Regenerate every affected Script 2 report in staging, compare against canonical reports, and publish only after one global approval.

    0.1 Mandatory Shared-Helper Architecture Audit And Remediation

    The pre-implementation audit found that, before the now-completed Phase F0 extraction (commit 18dd211), modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/reports.py contained approximately:

    4,801 lines
134 top-level functions
13 top-level classes
30 active core-test / Script 2 consumers
133 distinct directly imported symbols

    After the completed Phase F0 extraction, reports.py is 3,472 lines and no longer defines any moved value-parser, formatter, aggregation, Markdown, or report-artifact-I/O symbol; those families now live in their dedicated owners listed below. The numbers above are retained as the audit evidence that motivated the extraction.

    It also disables Pylint's too-many-lines check. Centralizing shared logic removed duplicated local helpers, but reports.py now owns unrelated responsibilities: value parsing, formatting, analytical calculations, Markdown rendering and legends, artifact I/O, CSV/parquet loading, DB queries, and typed report contracts.

    This plan must not deepen that god-module design.

    Ownership Rule

    Module ownership is determined by a complete semantic responsibility family, not by whether code is new or existing and not by a target line count.

    When new functionality belongs to the same family as existing reports.py functionality:

    1. move the complete coherent existing family to its correct owner;
    2. add the new functionality to that same owner;
    3. update every consumer directly in the same implementation change;
    4. delete the original definitions from reports.py;
    5. verify zero stale imports and references.

    If a complete family cannot be moved safely, do not split it between modules. Keep the family together until a complete migration is approved.

    Absolute rules:

    • No compatibility wrappers.
    • No deprecated aliases.
    • No import-and-re-export compatibility surfaces.
    • No duplicate definitions during or after migration.
    • No new investor, cross-fold, selectivity, Markdown, legend, or report-artifact formulas in reports.py.
    • A moved public symbol must be imported directly from its new owning module by every consumer.

    Immediate Complete-Family Extractions

    Semantic family New sole owner Existing definitions moved from reports.py New work added to owner
    Scalar value parsers and clamps modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/report_value_parsers.py safe_int, safe_float, safe_str, clamp_float, clamp_int None; stable low-level coercion owner reused by reports.py and report_metric_aggregations.py
    Display formatters and report display aliases modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/report_formatters.py FMT_NONE, scalar fmt_*, composite fmt_*, correlation display helpers, interpret_r, format_pipe_joined, and model/fold display alias helpers required by those formatters New investor/cross-fold display formatters only when they are pure value-to-string presentation helpers
    Report metric aggregation modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/report_metric_aggregations.py safe_percentage, safe_per_trade, mean_or_none, classify_proportionality Typed cross-fold, investor-summary, operational-rate, and Alpha RC selectivity aggregation
    Markdown tables and canonical legends modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/report_markdown.py Complete Markdown constants, legend registry/resolution, table rendering, header repetition, and enhance_markdown_tables family Every new canonical field legend
    Report artifact I/O modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/report_artifacts.py load_metadata, write_json, write_csv, write_atomic Staging/report artifact writes required by this plan
    Investor and backtest risk metrics modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/investor_metrics.py No same-family implementation currently identified in reports.py MTM curve, investor drawdown, daily risk, trade distribution, costs, turnover, exposure, and typed result/state contracts

    report_value_parsers.py is a dedicated low-level owner introduced so that report_metric_aggregations.py can reuse safe_float/safe_int without importing reports.py, which the forbidden dependency directions prohibit. Both reports.py and report_metric_aggregations.py import the scalar parsers from this owner; the owner depends on neither of them.

    The report-artifact family is moved together because write_atomic() applies Markdown enhancement for .md outputs. Its new owner may depend on report_markdown.py; reports.py must not remain the indirect owner of Markdown behavior.

    The display-formatter family is moved together because every exporter depends on the same canonical display contract for money, percentages, counts, model/fold labels, correlation labels, and composite table cells. Semantic wrappers such as fmt_sharpe, fmt_f1, and fmt_js remain first-class formatters, not dead aliases, because they encode the canonical display precision for specific report fields.

    modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/monetary_metrics.py is not part of this extraction. It is an already-existing owner of the existing monetary/friction formulas and is referenced later only because the new investor_metrics.py work sits beside it. No monetary/friction family is moved out of it and no new monetary formula is added to reports.py.

    Existing Families Retained In reports.py During This Plan

    The following families remain in reports.py until a later complete-family migration is separately planned:

    • JSON object parsers and CSV cell parsers (scalar value parsers and numeric clamps now live in report_value_parsers.py);
    • Script 2 summary CSV contracts and loaders;
    • trial, experiment, backtest-result, and model-profile report contracts;
    • DB-backed report fetchers;
    • prediction-parquet report adapters;
    • timestamp and report-identity utilities.

    This is not approval to add unrelated responsibilities to reports.py. Existing retained contracts may be extended only when the new field belongs to that existing contract family, such as adding persisted investor fields to a DB-backed session report record. Formulas and aggregations still belong to their dedicated owners.

    Required Migration Evidence

    Before metric implementation continues, the extraction change must provide:

    1. a complete pre-move definition and consumer inventory for each moved family;
    2. direct-import updates for every consumer and affected test;
    3. zero moved definitions remaining in reports.py;
    4. zero consumers importing moved symbols from reports.py;
    5. zero wrappers, aliases, or re-exports preserving the old import paths;
    6. focused parity tests proving moved existing behavior is unchanged;
    7. dedicated tests for each new owner;
    8. full quality gates for every moved owner and consumer.

    Cross-fold aggregation identities:

    • same_recipe_cross_fold: the same fold-invariant experiment recipe across folds;
    • best_per_fold_policy: a policy that independently selects one candidate per fold;
    • family_population: all candidates for a model family or tier summarized across folds;
    • ensemble_strategy: block + selector + pool/family + top_per_model + diversity + merge_rule.

    Required labeling:

    • Never call a cross-fold aggregate "the same model" unless the trained weights are identical.
    • Report cross_fold_identity, represented_folds, and fold_coverage beside every cross-fold aggregate.
    • Distinguish optimistic best_per_fold_policy results from fixed same_recipe_cross_fold results.

    Regime-conditional reporting (bull/bear and richer market-state splits) is intentionally not part of this cross-fold refactor. It is deferred to docs/plans/THESIS-SCRIPT2/20260529_SCRIPT2_MARKET_REGIME_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md, where it will be implemented properly with the real regime detector (scripts/analysis/regime/) — not from hard-coded fold numbers or a benchmark-return proxy. This plan delivers only the regime-agnostic cross-fold aggregation above.

    Investor-summary rules:

    • Investor base metrics are calculated by shared core/backfill helpers and persisted before reporting.
    • Reporters calculate only grouped summaries from persisted investor metrics and daily_returns_json.
    • Every grouped investor summary must expose its contributing observation count.
    • Cross-fold daily-risk summaries and worst-fold drawdown require exactly one selected session per represented fold. They do not apply to family_population or any group containing multiple sessions for the same fold.
    • Cross-fold daily-risk metrics use the merged daily-return distribution; they are not a continuous cross-fold equity curve and must not be used to invent cross-fold drawdown, recovery time, or Calmar.
    • Report exporters must consume one shared typed report-aggregation helper. They must not implement these formulas inline.

    3. Official Formulas

    All formulas must be implemented once in their owning shared typed helpers. Report exporters must consume persisted/helper-produced values and must not reimplement formulas inline.

    3.1 MTM Equity Foundation

    equity_mark_to_market(t)
  = cash(t)
  + unrealized_pnl_from_open_positions(t)

    Historical reconstruction:

    1. Start from session initial equity.
    2. Apply entry commissions at trade open.
    3. Mark every open position to the canonical session price series.
    4. Apply realized gross/net PnL and exit commissions at trade close.
    5. Validate reconstructed final values against persisted session totals before any write.

    Future runtime:

    • Update investor MTM risk state on every processed timestamp.
    • Keep existing operational/pruning drawdown behavior unchanged.
    • Do not rename existing operational drawdown contracts.
    • Persist the new investor metrics under explicit investor_mtm_* names.

    3.2 Investor Drawdown And Daily Risk

    New field Official formula Unit Null rule
    investor_mtm_max_drawdown max(running_peak_equity - equity_mark_to_market(t)) Money Null only when the MTM curve cannot be built.
    investor_mtm_max_drawdown_pct investor_mtm_max_drawdown / running_peak_equity_at_drawdown Ratio Null when peak equity is null or zero.
    investor_mtm_drawdown_duration_minutes Longest real-time interval below the previous MTM peak. Minutes Null when the MTM curve cannot be built.
    investor_mtm_recovery_time_minutes Longest real-time interval from drawdown start to recovery of the previous peak. Minutes Null when no drawdown recovers inside the session.
    daily_volatility Annualized standard deviation of UTC daily MTM returns: stdev(daily_returns) * sqrt(365). Ratio Null when fewer than two daily returns exist.
    sortino_daily Annualized daily Sortino: (mean_daily_return / downside_deviation_below_zero) * sqrt(365). Ratio Null when downside deviation is zero/unavailable or fewer than two daily returns exist.
    calmar_ratio Annualized MTM return divided by absolute investor MTM max drawdown percentage. Ratio Null when drawdown percentage is zero/unavailable or the session calendar span is too short to annualize.
    worst_day_return Minimum UTC daily MTM return. Ratio Null when no daily return exists.
    cvar_daily_95 Mean return in the worst 5% of UTC daily MTM returns. Ratio Null when fewer than twenty daily returns exist.

    Canonical daily return:

    daily_return(d)
  = last_equity_mark_to_market_in_utc_day(d)
  / first_equity_mark_to_market_in_utc_day(d)
  - 1

    Script 2 historical reconstruction uses the canonical 5m UTC price series. Durations are stored in real minutes, not tick counts or bar counts.

    Annualization and minimum-sample convention:

    • Daily-frequency risk metrics are annualized for an investor reading. Because Script 2 trades a 24/7 crypto market, the annualization base is 365 UTC days per year and the dispersion scaling factor is sqrt(365).
    • daily_volatility and sortino_daily annualization is pure unit scaling of realized daily statistics, not a forecast.
    • calmar_ratio uses the standard Calmar convention of annualized realized return over maximum drawdown. The return is annualized from the realized session return; it is reported only when the session calendar span supports annualization and is null otherwise.
    • The existing per-trade Sharpe ratio currently uses a trade-based sqrt(252) annualization base. Migrating that base from 252 (equities trading-day convention) to 365 (24/7 crypto convention) is tracked as a separate, out-of-scope follow-up with its own impact review in Section 12 and is not performed by the new-metrics phases here.
    • Minimum-sample thresholds: daily_volatility and sortino_daily require at least two daily returns; cvar_daily_95 requires at least twenty daily returns. Below threshold the metric is null, never a degraded value.
    current_mtm_return
  = (equity_mark_to_market - initial_equity) / initial_equity

annualized_mtm_return
  = (1 + current_mtm_return) ** (365 / session_calendar_days) - 1

calmar_ratio
  = annualized_mtm_return / abs(investor_mtm_max_drawdown_pct)

    Do not combine realized-only runtime return with investor MTM drawdown. Calmar is null until the investor MTM maximum drawdown percentage is positive and available, and until the session calendar span supports annualization.

    3.3 Trade Distribution

    New field Official formula Null rule
    profit_factor_net Sum of positive closed-trade net PnL divided by absolute sum of negative closed-trade net PnL. Null when no negative net PnL exists.
    profit_factor_gross Sum of positive closed-trade gross PnL divided by absolute sum of negative closed-trade gross PnL. Null when no negative gross PnL exists.
    avg_win_net Mean positive closed-trade net PnL. Null when no winning trade exists.
    avg_loss_net Absolute mean negative closed-trade net PnL. Null when no losing trade exists.
    payoff_ratio_net avg_win_net / avg_loss_net. Null when either input is unavailable or average loss is zero.

    Do not add a duplicate expectancy field. Existing per-trade values remain the official expectancy representation.

    3.4 Costs

    New field Official formula Null rule
    total_fees_paid Sum of entry and exit commissions. Zero only when complete trade data proves no fees.
    fees_per_trade total_fees_paid / closed_trade_count. Null when no closed trades exist.
    fees_to_gross_pnl_ratio total_fees_paid / abs(total_gross_pnl). Null when gross PnL is null or zero.
    total_slippage_paid Sum of exact execution slippage cost where a pre-slippage reference price exists. Null when exact historical reconstruction is unavailable.
    slippage_per_trade total_slippage_paid / closed_trade_count. Null when slippage is null or no closed trades exist.

    Unknown historical slippage must remain null. It must never be invented or silently converted to zero.

    3.5 Turnover And Exposure

    entry_notional = abs(size * entry_price)
exit_notional = abs(size * exit_price)
round_trip_notional = entry_notional + exit_notional
turnover_notional = sum(round_trip_notional)
turnover_ratio = turnover_notional / initial_equity
avg_trade_notional = mean(entry_notional)
    New field Official formula
    time_exposure_ratio Union duration with at least one open position divided by session duration.
    position_time_exposure_ratio Sum of each position's open duration divided by session duration. May exceed 1.0.
    capital_exposure_ratio MTM position-notional-time exposure divided by initial_equity * session_duration.

    capital_exposure_ratio is official only because this plan requires full MTM reconstruction. A frozen entry-notional approximation is not allowed.

    3.6 Operational Risk-Gate Counters

    proposal_blocked_count = sum(proposal_blocked_by_reason_json.values())
risk_manager_blocked_count = sum(entry_blocked_by_reason_json.values())
entry_blocked_count = proposal_blocked_count + risk_manager_blocked_count
entry_total_block_rate = entry_blocked_count / entry_candidate_signal_count
entry_risk_approval_rate = entry_approved_count / entry_attempt_count
entry_risk_block_rate = risk_manager_blocked_count / entry_attempt_count
risk_force_flat_rate = risk_force_flat_count / closed_trade_count

    Rates are null when their denominator is zero.

    Required typed reason codes:

    low_confidence
low_quality
position_scaling
risk_halt
cooldown
long_disabled
short_disabled
max_concurrent_positions
max_trades_per_day
non_positive_size
max_exposure
min_order_notional
max_drawdown_percent_stop
max_daily_loss

    Future runs use typed counters and reason maps. Historical reconstruction may use available typed state, exit reasons, session snapshots, and logs, but missing denied intents remain unknown rather than zero.

    3.7 Cross-Fold Aggregation

    Order represented folds chronologically before compounding.

    aggregate_net_pnl = sum(fold_net_pnl)
average_net_pnl = mean(fold_net_pnl)

aggregate_return = product(1 + fold_return) - 1
aggregate_benchmark_rc = product(1 + fold_benchmark_rc) - 1
aggregate_alpha_rc = aggregate_return - aggregate_benchmark_rc
average_alpha_rc = mean(fold_alpha_rc)

alpha_rc_fold_win_count = count(fold_alpha_rc > 0)
alpha_rc_fold_win_rate = alpha_rc_fold_win_count / fold_coverage

    Do not sum fold Alpha RC values and call the result aggregate Alpha RC. Alpha RC must be derived from the compounded strategy and benchmark returns for the represented folds.

    3.8 Alpha RC Selectivity

    delta_alpha_rc_vs_best_source
  = candidate_alpha_rc - best_source_alpha_rc

alpha_rc_improvement_pct_vs_best_source
  = delta_alpha_rc_vs_best_source / abs(best_source_alpha_rc)

proportionality_label_alpha_rc
  = classify_proportionality(
      trade_reduction_pct_vs_best_source,
      alpha_rc_improvement_pct_vs_best_source,
    )

    The shared classify_proportionality() terminology remains unchanged:

    • Better than proportional
    • Roughly proportional
    • Worse than proportional
    • NA

    The Alpha RC comparison is null/NA when the source Alpha RC is null or zero.

    3.9 Report-Calculated Investor Summaries

    Report-calculated investor summaries consume persisted session/fold metrics. They do not recalculate the underlying MTM equity curve, trade distribution, costs, turnover, or exposure.

    For each median summary:

    investor_summary_observation_count
  = count(non_null_persisted_metric_values)

median_<metric>
  = median(non_null_persisted_metric_values)

    worst_fold_investor_mtm_max_drawdown_pct
  = max(non_null_fold_investor_mtm_max_drawdown_pct)

    The maximum is used because investor MTM drawdown is persisted as a positive loss magnitude.

    For cross-fold daily-risk summaries:

    1. Verify the aggregate identity contains exactly one selected session per represented fold.
    2. Load each represented fold's persisted daily_returns_json.
    3. Merge daily return observations in UTC-date order.
    4. Reject duplicate UTC dates inside one aggregate identity rather than silently double-counting them.
    5. Calculate:
    cross_fold_daily_volatility
  = standard_deviation(merged_daily_returns) * sqrt(365)

cross_fold_sortino_daily
  = (mean(merged_daily_returns)
     / downside_deviation_below_zero(merged_daily_returns)) * sqrt(365)

cross_fold_worst_day_return
  = min(merged_daily_returns)

cross_fold_cvar_daily_95
  = mean(worst_5_percent_of_merged_daily_returns)

    The Section 3.2 annualization base (365) and minimum-sample thresholds apply to the merged distribution: cross_fold_daily_volatility and cross_fold_sortino_daily require at least two merged daily returns, and cross_fold_cvar_daily_95 requires at least twenty merged daily returns.

    The underlying shared daily-risk helper and its existing null rules remain authoritative. The merged daily-return distribution does not create one continuous investable equity curve because fold sessions reset capital independently. Therefore, do not derive cross-fold drawdown, recovery time, or Calmar from it.

    If an aggregate contains multiple sessions for the same fold, cross-fold daily-risk summaries and worst_fold_investor_mtm_max_drawdown_pct are not eligible and must not be rendered. Group-level medians remain valid because they summarize the population without pretending it is one strategy path.

    4. Schema And Persistence Contract

    4.1 Manual DB Migration Policy

    • SQL migrations are manual.
    • Show exact SQL to Manu before execution.
    • Execute only after explicit approval.
    • Add nullable columns without defaults.
    • Verify schema before any backfill.
    • Run backfill dry-run before write mode.
    • Do not overwrite existing non-null values without an explicit overwrite approval.

    Reconciliation with the closure plan: SCRIPT2_CLOSURE_AND_NEW_ENSEMBLE_PLAN.md states "The DB schema is not refactored." That statement is scoped to the ensemble campaign work, which attaches results through the existing trial-centric schema and adds no columns. It does not forbid this plan's additive, nullable, no-default column additions to backtest_sessions and trials. The two are compatible: the closure plan changes no schema, and this plan only adds nullable columns that existing ensemble queries ignore. No existing column is altered or removed.

The reason maps and the daily-return map live only inside operational_gates / daily_risk in the JSON — they have no flat column.     • Do not add blocked entry rows to trades.
    • Do not add new trade columns in this implementation wave.

    • Do not change live_sessions, events, or execution_plans in the Script 2 migration.

    4.6 Nullable Versus Required Field Policy

    A new field is Optional/NULL only when it can be genuinely null. A field that will hold a value in every session must not stay Optional merely to tolerate the create-then-backfill window.

    • Genuinely nullable (Optional/None permanently): every field whose Section 3.2–3.6 null rule can fire — e.g. total_slippage_paid / slippage_per_trade (unreconstructable historical slippage), calmar_ratio, cvar_daily_95, sortino_daily / daily_volatility (sessions shorter than the sample thresholds), the profit-factor / payoff fields (no losing/winning trade), investor_mtm_recovery_time_minutes (drawdown never recovered), and every operational counter that remains PARTIAL_APPROX historically. These stay nullable in the DB and Optional in the typed models permanently.
    • ~~Always present (tighten after backfill)~~ — SUPERSEDED (see Final decision below): the original intent was to tighten fields like total_fees_paid / turnover_notional / time_exposure_ratio / investor_mtm_max_drawdown to required after F4. This was closed as won't-do (2026-06-11) — the F4 coverage audit showed even these have legitimate NULLs (e.g. interrupted/never-progressed sessions), so they stay Optional. Kept for history only.
    • ~~Tightening mechanics~~ — SUPERSEDED: the SQLite NOT NULL table-rebuild described here is not performed (won't-do, 2026-06-11). The engine/backfill still always write a value for the always-present fields on a normal run; the schema simply stays nullable.
    • ~~Final per-field split~~ — SUPERSEDED: the F4 coverage audit (audit doc §6) is the final per-field result; the conclusion is "all Optional" (no tightening).
    • TypeScript coherence: every DB column / Pydantic field change that the control panel surfaces must also update the frontend TypeScript types (modules/control-panel/frontend/src/types/backtests.ts, trials.ts, and their consumers under frontend/src/lib and frontend/src/components). A schema change is not complete until the Python model, the SQL column, and the TS types all agree.
    • Final decision (2026-06-11): all new flat fields stay Optional — no NOT NULL tightening. The backfill ran and the DB coverage audit proved every NULL is an exact §3 null-rule firing (not a gap): NULL is a valid output of the current engine for ordinary runs (no losing/winning trade, sub-threshold daily samples, 0 closed trades, drawdown never recovered, interrupted-before-progress), so a NOT NULL constraint would be wrong regardless of the orphan rows. The 8 operational gate counters are 100% null on historical sessions; populating the derivable subset is DONE (risk_force_flat_count backfilled = 0 on 9166 sessions; the 7 no-trace counters stay null by design, no re-run; §6.6) — that changes their values, not the schema nullability; new runs already emit them. Closes the §13.7.6 tightening question (separate from the counter backfill). Detail: docs/audit/20260610_1642_METRICS_LEARNINGS_AUDIT.md §6.

    5. Engine And Shared-Code Implementation

    5.1 Shared Helper Architecture

    The Section 0.1 architecture remediation is the first implementation wave. New metric implementation cannot begin until the existing-family extractions are complete and validated.

    Primary shared targets:

    • modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/monetary_metrics.py
    • modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/investor_metrics.py
    • modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/report_value_parsers.py

    • modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/report_metric_aggregations.py

    • modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/reports.py
    • modules/core/src/rainbow/core/services/backtest_session_service.py
    • typed BacktestMetrics, TrialSummaryMetrics, runtime snapshot, and resume-state contracts

    Ownership:

    • Low-level scalar value parsers (safe_int, safe_float, safe_str) and numeric clamps (clamp_float, clamp_int) belong in report_value_parsers.py.
    • Pure value-to-display formatters, semantic field formatters, composite cell formatters, correlation display labels, and model/fold display aliases belong in report_formatters.py.
    • Existing monetary/friction formulas remain in monetary_metrics.py.
    • MTM curve, investor drawdown, daily risk, trade distribution, costs, turnover, and exposure formulas belong in investor_metrics.py.
    • Cross-fold, investor-summary, operational-rate, and Alpha RC selectivity formulas belong in report_metric_aggregations.py.
    • Canonical legends and Markdown table transformation/rendering belong in report_markdown.py.
    • Report artifact reads/writes belong in report_artifacts.py.

    5.7 Live-Running Impact To Investigate (mandatory pre-F2 gate)

    There is live-running related code in the repository, and some metric names overlap with concepts that could matter in live mode.     §5.7 Findings (verified 2026-06-06)

    • Live-trading runner: no impact. modules/live-trading-runner/src imports nothing from rainbow.backtesting_engine and never uses BacktestMetrics, BacktestSessionService, update_backtest_session, backtest_sessions, investor_metrics, or report_metric_aggregations. The live runner is fully decoupled from backtest session/metrics persistence, so F2/F3/F4 do not touch it.
    • Control-panel: safe, with one hard constraint. control_panel/services/backtest_service.py reads the persisted payload via BacktestMetrics.model_validate(...). BacktestMetrics (rainbow.model_trainer.types) is a Pydantic model whose convention is "all fields required, no defaults" but which has no extra="forbid" (Pydantic default is extra="ignore"). Therefore: (a) the JSON-only keys (daily_returns_json, reason maps) are safely ignored by control-panel; (b) every NEW BacktestMetrics / Stage-3 field added in F2 MUST be Optional with a default of None, otherwise model_validate would fail on historical sessions whose JSON predates the new keys (and on sessions whose values stay null by the plan's null rules). This overrides the model's historical "all required" convention for the new nullable investor/operational fields only.
    • DB columns: additive NULL-able columns are safe for every SQL reader (control-panel selects included).
    • No TypeScript surface: the control panel here is Python (rainbow.control_panel); no TS types reference these fields.
    • Conclusion: F2 may proceed. New typed BacktestMetrics / trial Stage-3 fields are added as Optional/None; engine MetricsSnapshot additions keep defaults so no existing constructor call breaks.

    6. Historical Backfill Implementation

    6.1 Per-Session Workflow

    Eligibility (Manu, 2026-06-08): ALL backtest sessions in the DB — no status filter (not just COMPLETED) and no thesis/Script-2 filter. The whole backtest_sessions table is backfilled. Sessions with no closed trades or no recoverable price coverage produce a null/empty investor block and are recorded explicitly, never skipped silently (a session that never traded is legitimately null — this is independent of the eligibility scope, and the Section 4.6 NOT NULL question is deferred to §13.7.6 regardless).

    For every backtest session:

    1. Load session identity, range, initial equity, trial link, and current metric payload.
    2. Load closed trades with timestamps, side, size, prices, PnL, and commissions.
    3. Resolve the session's canonical historical price series.
    4. Reconstruct the 5m UTC MTM equity and position timeline.
    5. Calculate all backfillable new investor, distribution, cost, turnover, and exposure metrics.
    6. Reconstruct operational counters from typed state, exit reasons, snapshots, and logs where available.
    7. Mark operational metrics PARTIAL_APPROX when denied-intent history is incomplete.
    8. Validate reconstructed totals against persisted session totals.
    9. Produce a dry-run result without writing.
    10. In approved write mode, update session columns, session JSON, trial mirrors, and Stage 3 JSON transactionally.

    6.2 Safety Contract

    • Mandatory on-disk DB backup: before any write-mode execution, create a physical copy of the SQLite database file on disk and confirm it exists. No backfill write starts without a verified fresh backup.
    • Dry-run is the default.
    • Writes are idempotent.
    • Each session update is transactional.
    • Existing non-null new metric fields are not overwritten without an explicit flag.
    • Missing historical information remains null, never silently zero.
    • Failed sessions produce explicit skip/failure reasons.
    • The backfill produces counts by reconstructed, skipped, failed, and written.

    6.3 Completeness Meaning

    Completeness value Meaning
    YES New metric family was reconstructed using the official formula and required historical inputs.
    PARTIAL_APPROX Best available historical reconstruction was performed, but exact future-runtime parity is impossible.
    NO Required historical evidence is unavailable; affected values remain null.

    6.4 Batched Price-Series Reuse (efficiency)

    The expensive part of the backfill is loading the canonical 5m UTC price series for thousands of sessions. Sessions that share the same (symbol, timeframe, date-range) share the same price series, so prices are loaded once and reused; only the per-session trade replay differs.

    1. Group eligible sessions by a price-series key (symbol, timeframe, start, end).
    2. For each group, load the 5m UTC price series once into an in-memory timestamp→price structure.
    3. For each session in the group, replay only that session's own closed trades against the shared price series: build the MTM equity and open-position timeline (equity_mtm(t) = realized(t) + Σ unrealized(open positions marked at price[t])), then feed the shared InvestorRuntimeState accumulators.
    4. Sample the MTM curve at the same 5m cadence the live engine used, so path-dependent drawdown duration/recovery and the capital-exposure time integral reproduce exactly.

    Rationale: the price load is shared across the group (avoids re-reading the same parquet N times); the per-session trade replay is cheap because trades are few relative to candles. No silent caps: log group sizes, sessions skipped, and any session whose window lacks shared price coverage.

    6.5 Golden Re-Run Validation (authoritative correctness gate)

    The strongest proof that an artifact-only backfill reproduces "what the engine would have produced". It validates a sample only (NOT all sessions — re-running everything would defeat the backfill); a representative 10–30 sessions spanning symbols, timeframes, date-ranges, trial profiles, and trade counts is enough to exercise every metric path with confidence.

    Concrete protocol (reuses the extra_backtests engine-run machinery — BacktestingEngine.run_with_trial + load_backtest_session_metrics_from_db):

    1. Pick the stratified sample of trials/sessions.
    2. For each, run the trial through the current engine (run_with_trial) — which produces the investor block in finalize (attach_investor_metrics) — yielding both the engine BacktestMetrics (ground truth, in-memory; no F2.5 persistence needed) and that run's trades.
    3. Run the backfill reconstruction on that same run's trades + price series → backfill BacktestMetrics.
    4. Compare backfill vs engine field-by-field within a float tolerance. Any mismatch beyond tolerance is a hard failure that blocks the write.

    Comparing on the fresh run's own trades (not the old stored trades) isolates exactly artifact-reconstruction == engine-live-accumulation and avoids re-execution non-determinism (old trades vs re-generated trades). The fresh run supplies both the trades and the engine metrics, so the test is apples-to-apples.

    This is complemented by, not replaced by:

    • Structural parity: the backfill calls the same InvestorRuntimeState accumulators as the engine (not a re-implementation), so formula divergence is impossible by construction.
    • Reconciliation/property tests: Σ fees == total_fees_paid; Σ net_pnl == the existing total_net_pnl (cross-check against an already-persisted column); max_drawdown ≥ 0; exposure ratios ∈ [0, 1].

    6.6 Reproducibility Scope (resolved 2026-06-11)

    Correction (2026-06-11): the previous wording claimed a closed decision (Manu, 2026-06-08): backfill-only, no mass re-execution. Manu never made that decision — it was a misattribution and is removed. Verified data fact (checked 2026-06-11): the operational gate counters left no per-tick persisted trace (trades, per-trade entry_reason, and the events table hold only executed-trade decisions / migrations; exit codes are only STOP_LOSS/TAKE_PROFIT/SIGNAL_FLIP), so an artifact backfill can recover only the derivable subset; the denied-intent counters (candidates / proposal-blocks / attempts / approvals / entry-blocks / halts) have no trace. The F2.3 producer is built (both engines emit them for new runs).

    Decision (Manu, 2026-06-11): do the operational-counter backfill as best as possible — but NO re-run of the backtests. DONE 2026-06-11. A single best-effort artifact backfill of whatever IS derivable from persisted artifacts, run with the standard backfill flow (dry-run → mandatory on-disk DB backup → idempotent transactional write → post-write consistency checks):

    • Derivable subset (DONE 2026-06-11): risk_force_flat_count is derived per session from the trades (count of closed trades whose exit_reason.code == RISK_FORCE_FLAT) — exact, and it derives to 0 everywhere (zero such closes in the whole DB; verified over 2.16M closed trades). Backfilled to 0 on the 9166 sessions with a payload and mirrored to the 2410 trials' stage3_risk_force_flat_count. No completeness marker is written — the backfill-provenance fields were removed (see §1.2 note).
    • Denied-intent counters (candidates / proposal-blocks / attempts / approvals / entry-blocks): they left no persisted trace, so they stay NULL — never reconstructed, never fabricated, and the backtests are NOT re-run. Only new runs populate them (the F2.3 producer is built).

    Reproducibility tiers:

    Tier Metrics Backfill reproducibility
    Exact Investor drawdown / daily risk / calmar / cvar / worst-day, trade distribution, fees, turnover, exposure 100% — deterministic from persisted trades + 5m price series + shared accumulators.
    Exact-if-present total_slippage_paid, slippage_per_trade 100% per trade when the structured execution metadata exists. Verified: a real trade's exit_reason.meta.execution carries price_before_slippage / slippage_percent / slippage_amount. F4's dry-run measures coverage; trades lacking it stay null (never zero).
    Backfill DONE (best-effort artifact, NO re-run) Operational proposal/entry/halt/force-flat counters + reason maps No per-tick artifact trace. The best-effort artifact backfill set the only derivable counter — risk_force_flat_count = 0 (exact; zero force-flat closes in the DB) — on sessions + trials; the denied-intent counters stay null (no trace; not re-run; new runs emit them — the F2.3 producer is built). See the boxed decision above.

    Consequence for Section 4.6: the NOT-NULL tightening is closed (won't-do, 2026-06-11) — every new field stays Optional because NULL is a valid engine output (the §3 null-rules; see §4.6 / §13.7.6). Populating the operational counters (above) changes their values for historical sessions, not their schema nullability.

    7.4 Ensemble Source-Trial Alpha RC Repair

    The ensemble results.json/results.csv source_results rows historically carry alpha_rc and benchmark_return_rc as null even when the underlying stage-3 trial has Risk-Constrained values persisted in the DB. Root cause: the original_stage3 source-baseline builder in scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/ensemble_backtests/run_ensemble_backtests.py copied only the classical alpha and benchmark_return from the stage-3 backtest_sessions row and omitted alpha_risk_constrained / benchmark_return_risk_constrained. It is a field-copy omission, not missing data (the DB stage-3 row holds both).

    Required steps:

    1. Writer fix (future runs): DONE. The original_stage3 source builder now copies benchmark_return_risk_constrained and alpha_risk_constrained from the stage-3 session, so all newly generated source_results carry RC. The RC parameters are required keyword-only, so a future call-site omission is also caught by the type checkers, and scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/tests/test_run_ensemble_source_rc.py locks the runtime behaviour (RC passed through, null preserved when the DB has none).
    2. Existing artifacts (repair): DONE. For already-generated ensemble campaigns, either (a) regenerate the campaign reports — the regeneration in Section 8.2.6 then carries RC — or (b) when only re-rendering from existing results.json, enrich each source_results RC from the DB by backtest_session_id (present in every source row) instead of trusting the artifact null. Never invent RC; read it from the authoritative DB row. Executed via path (b) for the 6 active non-legacy batch roots (504 campaigns): the source_results alpha_rc/benchmark_return_rc and the pairwise delta_alpha_rc/delta_benchmark_return_rc in every results.json/results.csv/comparisons.csv were filled from the DB; a backfill tool and an only-RC-changed verifier live under scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/refactor/tools/.
    3. Any RC-based ensemble comparison (delta_alpha_rc_vs_best_source, better-than-proportional Alpha RC) must read source RC through this DB-enriched path, never from the raw artifact null.

    8.2.6 Ensemble campaign reports (all active non-legacy campaigns)

    Each batch root produces TWO report kinds, both regenerated: the campaign-level campaign_report.md (audit_ensemble_batch_results.py) and the per-campaign report.md for every execution (render_ensemble_backtest_report.py). The 6 active non-legacy batch roots below were verified on disk (2026-06-12): 504 per-campaign report.md (96 + 96 + 72 + 72 + 72 + 96) plus 6 campaign_report.md.

    # All 6 active non-legacy batch roots (verified on disk 2026-06-12).
ENSEMBLE_BATCH_ROOTS=(
  20260521_154249_phase1_block_a_friction
  20260526_114000_phase1_block_a_promise
  20260527_015750_phase1_block_b_promise
  20260527_042255_phase1_block_b_friction
  20260528_024240_phase1_block_b_promise_rc
  20260528_115524_phase1_block_a_promise_rc
)
ENS_ROOT="scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/ensemble_backtests/results"

for batch in "${ENSEMBLE_BATCH_ROOTS[@]}"; do
  # (a) Campaign-level campaign_report.md — DB-enriched by backtest_session_id (explicit --db-path).
  .venv/bin/python scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/ensemble_backtests/audit_ensemble_batch_results.py \
    --batch-dir "$ENS_ROOT/$batch" \
    --db-path database/rainbow_trader.sqlite \
    --output-dir "$STAGE_ROOT/ensemble_backtests/results/$batch"

  # (b) Per-campaign report.md for every execution — DB auto-resolved from the artifact db_path metadata.
  while IFS= read -r results_csv; do
    rel="${results_csv#"$ENS_ROOT"/}"
    .venv/bin/python scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/ensemble_backtests/render_ensemble_backtest_report.py \
      --results-csv "$results_csv" \
      --output-md "$STAGE_ROOT/ensemble_backtests/results/${rel%/results.csv}/report.md"
  done < <(find "$ENS_ROOT/$batch" -mindepth 2 -name results.csv -not -path '*_LEGACY*')
done

    No --db-as-of-completed-at applies here: ensemble enrichment reads specific sessions by backtest_session_id, not a completion-time window, so there is no later-completed-row leak to cut (unlike the per-run progress packs in §8.2.3).

    Every active non-legacy ensemble report is regenerated like every other report — none is left out. The only coordination is timing, not exclusion: SCRIPT2_CLOSURE_AND_NEW_ENSEMBLE_PLAN.md Block B (promise_rc batches B2b, B3c, B4b) is still producing new batches, so regenerate each ensemble report from its settled batch results and re-run the regeneration for any batch the closure plan lands after this pass. Re-derive ENSEMBLE_BATCH_ROOTS from disk at regeneration time if the closure plan has landed further batches since 2026-06-12.

    The source-trial Alpha RC enrichment gap applies here: the ensemble results.json source_results rows carry alpha_rc/benchmark_return_rc as null even when the underlying trial has Risk-Constrained values in the DB (the ensemble writer only mapped the classical alpha/benchmark_return). Any RC-based ensemble comparison must read the Risk-Constrained values from the DB by backtest_session_id, which is present in each source row, rather than trusting the artifact's null.

    The commands above are the complete non-legacy regeneration set. Do not run ad-hoc partial command sets. Never read from or write over _LEGACY / *_LEGACY_PRE_RC.md artifacts.

    9. Manual SQL Review And Execution

    Before SQL execution:

    1. Create a mandatory on-disk backup copy of the SQLite database file and confirm it exists.
    2. Compare the SQL in Section 4 against the actual current DB schema.
    3. Confirm every proposed column is new.
    4. Confirm all new columns are nullable and have no default.
    5. Show the final SQL to Manu.
    6. Execute only after explicit approval.
    7. Run PRAGMA table_info(backtest_sessions) and PRAGMA table_info(trials).
    8. Confirm the new columns exist and historical values remain null before backfill.

    No Alembic migration is required for this work.

    10.1 Phased Execution Gates

    Implementation proceeds in ordered phases. Each phase has a hard gate. A later phase must not start until the previous gate passes.

    Testing cadence: each phase runs only its own targeted tests plus per-file quality gates (py_compile, ruff, mypy --strict, pyright, pylint). The complete pytest suite is slow (it takes hours), so it is run once at the end, as part of Phase F5 acceptance — never per phase.

    • Phase F0 — Architecture extraction. ✅ COMPLETE (commit 18dd211, verified 2026-06-06). Extract the report formatter, aggregation, Markdown, and report-artifact families from reports.py, migrate every consumer directly, and pass parity plus ownership tests (Sections 0.1 and 5.1). Gate: zero moved definitions in reports.py, zero stale old-path imports, zero wrappers or re-exports, all parity and ownership tests green, and full quality gates on every moved owner and consumer.
    • Phase F1 — Shared helpers, typed contracts, and formulas. ✅ COMPLETE. investor_metrics and all report_metric_aggregations cross-fold, investor-summary, cross-fold daily-risk, Alpha-RC-selectivity, and operational-rate formulas (Sections 3.6–3.9) are implemented with typed frozen-dataclass results and unit tests. Regime-conditional reporting is deferred to the regime plan (Section 1.1). Gate passed: every formula and null rule tested, quality gates green, no DB or engine change.
    • Phase F2 — Engine runtime, pause/resume, and persistence. Complete the Section 5.7 live-running impact investigation before starting this phase. Wire runtime accumulators, snapshot/final persistence, session columns/JSON, and trial mirrors.     13.7.2 Corrected design decision: investor_metrics DOES apply to live; rng does NOT

    Earlier wording assumed the live shell would carry investor_metrics: null. That was wrong (Manu corrected it). Evidence:

    • Live already produces a per-tick equity curve and PnL totals: modules/live-trading-runner/.../helpers/instance_manager.py (accounting_snapshot.timestamp, .equity, .realized_pnl_total, .unrealized_pnl_total, .open_positions_count, .closed_trades_count).
    • The investor accumulators (InvestorDrawdownAccumulator, DailyReturnsAccumulator) live in modules/core/.../investor_metrics.py and are session-type-agnostic: they consume (timestamp, equity).
    • Therefore live can and must compute investor metrics (drawdown, daily returns) the same way backtest does. The live shell must NOT store investor_metrics: null.

    rng is the only genuinely backtest-only field: verified there is no rng / getstate / setstate / runtime-seed state in the live (non-_OLD/) code; live uses only prediction_seed (model seed, not runtime RNG state). Live is real-time and does not reproduce via a seeded RNG, so live's shell has no rng.

    Rule (Manu, strict): no null placeholders in the live shell. Define purpose-built types instead.

Done as a standalone in-place ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN (SQLite 3.35+, no full table rebuild needed) via scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/refactor/tools/drop_legacy_resume_columns.py --apply (timestamped backup ..._drop_legacy_resume_backup_20260610T165915Z). Pre-conditions all proven: strict-legacy coverage check PASS (9144 backtest rows, live 0), zero code readers/writers (resume reads runtime_state_json), ORM attrs removed, export_persistence_fields() reduced to a 3-tuple, database suite + per-file gates green.

    NOT NULL tightening — CLOSED, won't-do (2026-06-11). The new investor/gate flat fields stay Optional: NULL is a valid output of the current engine, proven field-by-field by the §3 null-rules (a normal correct run leaves NULL whenever a rule fires — no losing trade, < 2 / < 20 daily returns, 0 closed trades, drawdown never recovered, run interrupted before progress). A NOT NULL constraint would be violated by ordinary runs, independent of the 4 never-progressed orphans. The DB coverage audit confirms every NULL equals its exact null-rule population (e.g. 30 = no-trade sessions, 52 = no-loser, 97 = no-winner). Historical gate counters are final under the approved null-honesty rule: the derivable subset is backfilled, no-trace denied-intent counters stay NULL → NA, no historical re-run is performed, and new runs emit the full counters. Detail: docs/audit/20260610_1642_METRICS_LEARNINGS_AUDIT.md §6.

    Only after Phase B (live switch + backtest service cleanup) proves zero readers/writers of the legacy JSON columns in BOTH backtest and live:

    • Kept the three flat fields (risk_manager_daily_pnl, risk_manager_date, risk_manager_halted).
